## Grids and geometry evidence {#sec-ch15-ch03-tests}

### Summary

A grid can be wrong in two different ways. The metric of one block (its face areas, volumes and curvature
sources) can disagree with the formulas of @sec-ch03, or every block can be right on its own while the blocks
disagree with each other where they meet. This section collects the tests that check both for the grids and
the exchange of @sec-ch03: analytic metric comparisons, bitwise agreement of a decomposed grid with the whole,
and conservation across panel seams and column splits. Each row names the test, what it asserts and the
tolerance its author chose.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Ties the chapter 3 claims (metrics, decomposition, seams, column splits) to eight registered tests.

**Data.** Face coordinates, areas, volumes and conserved totals of the fixtures; tolerances read from the source.

**Placement.** Verification outside the simulation step, in a build at the code pin.

**Activation.** Select the tests by their ctest name; the seam arms are set by their registration's environment.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact face agreement in one process is not conservation across ranks.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch15-ch03-tests-assertions.
:::

Local symbols: none; `got` and `want` are the test's face-coordinate
arrays [m], `ng` its ghost-cell count and `ix2` its dimensionless cell offset.

The eight tests fall into three groups: the metric of one block against reference formulas and exact
integrals, the equality of a decomposed grid with the undecomposed one, and the conservation of totals across
cubed-sphere panel seams and $x_1$ column splits, in one process and across two ranks.

### Derivation

Why the catalogue reads these tests the way it does, each step tied to the source at the pin.

1. *Separate metric accuracy from decomposition consistency.*
   `SphericalPolar.geometry_matches_athena_reference_formulas`
   ({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp SphericalPolar.geometry_matches_athena_reference_formulas >}}) compares
   cell centres, face areas, volumes and the curvature sources with closed-form references by `allclose` at
   rtol = atol = $10^{-12}$: a tolerance, because the formulas are evaluated in a different order.
2. *Require equality where the code promises it.*
   `CoordinateDecomposition.blocks_match_the_undecomposed_grid_bitwise`
   ({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateDecomposition.blocks_match_the_undecomposed_grid_bitwise >}})
   slices the whole-grid faces with each block's offset and compares by `torch::equal`; the block faces are
   the same numbers, so one differing bit is a failure. `CubedSphere.subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block`
   ({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp CubedSphere.subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block >}})
   makes the same demand of faces, spacings and density after one stage for 1, 2 and 4 blocks per panel edge.
3. *Read an exact-integral row as a relative tolerance.*
   `RadialFaceMoments.closed_forms_match_the_exact_integrals`
   ({{< code tests/test_radial_face_moments.cpp RadialFaceMoments.closed_forms_match_the_exact_integrals >}})
   accepts the face-centroid shift and second moment within relative $10^{-14}$ in the tabulated cases;
   `one_value_per_cell_on_a_multi_cell_column` instead uses absolute $10^{-14}$
   ({{< code tests/test_radial_face_moments.cpp RadialFaceMoments.one_value_per_cell_on_a_multi_cell_column >}}).
4. *Read a seam row as a budget.* `arm_conservation`
   ({{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py arm_conservation >}}) forms volume-weighted totals over six
   panels and requires their relative drift below `DRIFT_TOL` $= 10^{-12}$, the ratio form of @sec-ch15; the
   same script requires a rest state to stay below `REST_TOL` $= 10^{-9}$ in $|v|/c_s$ and the on/off arms to
   differ by at least `DIFF_TOL` $= 10^{-13}$, so that an ignored switch fails.
5. *Read a column-split row by its arm.* `radial_exact_split_gap`
   ({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp radial_exact_split_gap >}}) compares a column split into two blocks
   with one block at three resolutions. With the corrected-PE[^rg-5f3883a5bbdd] work on, the gap must be exactly zero and the
   split column's energy drift at most $10^{-13}$; with it off, the gap may be round-off, at most $10^{-13}$.
   Across two ranks, `X1SeamSplitMp.split_across_two_ranks_matches_one_process`
   ({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split_mp.cpp X1SeamSplitMp.split_across_two_ranks_matches_one_process >}})
   bounds the gap to the in-process split and to one block by $10^{-13}$ each, and the drift by $10^{-13}$
   with the switch on.

The round-off bound of @sec-ch15 covers the reductions inside the budget rows; the equality rows have no
tolerance to widen.

### Numerical method

Read the assertion and its registration, then run the selection in a build configured from the code pin
(@fig-ch15-evidence, @sec-ch15). The `X1SeamSplit` arms are separate ctest entries that set a switch in the
test's environment and require exactly one passing case ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}); the two-rank
arms launch the executable with `torchrun` and two processes. Record device, precision, process count and
every skip separately.

: Assertions this catalogue reads. {#tbl-ch15-ch03-tests-sources}

**How to select the tests.** From the repository root, with `build` the directory configured from the code pin,
list the selection and then run it:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_coordinate\.release$'
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -R '^test_coordinate\.release$'
```

The other rows are selected the same way:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_radial_face_moments\.release$'
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_cubed_sphere_cell_volume_python$'
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_cubed_sphere_exchange\.release$'
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_flux_covariance_seams_python$'
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_x1_seam_split_radial_exact\.release$'
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_x1_seam_split_mp_radial_exact\.release$'
```

Run each listed selection with `--output-on-failure` in place of `-N`. The decomposition case builds its options in C++ and has no YAML switch; the seam and split arms take
their switch from the registration, so set nothing by hand. A test executable must run from the configured
build so its sibling cases find their fixtures; an empty selection prints "No tests were found!!!" and is not a
result (@sec-ch15).

The contract of the decomposition case, from
`CoordinateDecomposition.blocks_match_the_undecomposed_grid_bitwise`
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp CoordinateDecomposition.blocks_match_the_undecomposed_grid_bitwise >}}):

```cpp
auto got = blk->x2f.narrow(0, ng, op->nx2() + 1);
auto want = ref->x2f.narrow(0, ng + op->ix2(), op->nx2() + 1);
EXPECT_TRUE(torch::equal(got, want));
```

The first slice is the block's owned faces, the second the matching faces of the whole grid; `torch::equal`
demands zero discrepancy, a stronger condition than any tolerance of @sec-ch15.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_coordinate.release` | the spherical-polar metric matches the reference formulas | rtol = atol = $10^{-12}$ | the test |
| `test_coordinate.release` | decomposed faces reproduce the undecomposed grid | exact (`torch::equal`) | the test |
| `test_radial_face_moments.release` | face-centroid shift and second moment match the exact integrals | relative $10^{-14}$ | the test |
| `test_cubed_sphere_cell_volume_python` | shell volumes sum to the exact value; a rest state stays at rest; no step is rejected | `REST_TOL` $= 10^{-6}$ in $|v|/c_s$ | the script |
| `test_cubed_sphere_exchange.release` | 2 and 4 blocks per panel edge agree with 1 after a stage | exact (`torch::equal`) | the test |
| `test_flux_covariance_seams_python` | six-panel totals are conserved; rest holds; the switch acts | drift $<10^{-12}$; rest $<10^{-9}$; difference $\ge10^{-13}$ | `DRIFT_TOL`, `REST_TOL`, `DIFF_TOL` |
| `test_x1_seam_split_radial_exact.release` | the split column equals one block and its energy budget closes | gap exactly 0; drift $\le10^{-13}$ | the test |
| `test_x1_seam_split_mp_radial_exact.release` | two ranks agree with the in-process split and with one block | gaps $\le10^{-13}$; drift $\le10^{-13}$ | the test |

: Acceptance criteria at the code pin; CPU run evidence is recorded below, with CUDA coverage limited explicitly. {#tbl-ch15-ch03-tests-assertions}

The seam script's entry point is `main` ({{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py main >}}) and its
thresholds are the three module constants ({{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py DRIFT_TOL >}}). The
switch-off arm of the column split, `test_x1_seam_split_radial_exact_off.release`, runs the same assertion
with the gap bounded by $10^{-13}$ instead of exact equality and no drift assertion. The report-only
`src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py` checks the radial moments, the spherical-polar identities, the
gnomonic transforms, the Morton order, the interpolation slide bound and the face-state suffix rule (`[C20]`)
on ports and imports no snapy.

The coordinate executable holds both the analytic metric comparison and the exact decomposition check.
Exact face agreement in one process says nothing about conservation across communicating ranks; the
seam and two-rank rows cover that.[^ch15-ch03-run]

### Limits

A panel subdivision in one process is not a multi-process result. The selected tests do not establish every
corner stencil or every curvature source, and the slide bound of the report check does not execute the
exchange. Configurations that need runtime evidence are listed in @sec-ch12-matrix.
